### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d73c1d618e3eede73eb71f647bb6ac1b8bfbb2c`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d73c1d618e3eede73eb71f647bb6ac1b8bfbb2c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bfaa1afe3e3a243a0fc29de63cf6abb17a97a923` — the merge of head `332beed051a7138b53c5b0afa3c020fd1190c027` into base `3d73c1d618e3eede73eb71f647bb6ac1b8bfbb2c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bfaa1afe3e3a243a0fc29de63cf6abb17a97a923 && git checkout bfaa1afe3e3a243a0fc29de63cf6abb17a97a923
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3d73c1d618e3eede73eb71f647bb6ac1b8bfbb2c 332beed051a7138b53c5b0afa3c020fd1190c027 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3d73c1d618e3eede73eb71f647bb6ac1b8bfbb2c && git merge --no-ff 332beed051a7138b53c5b0afa3c020fd1190c027

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d73c1d618e3eede73eb71f647bb6ac1b8bfbb2c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3d73c1d618e3eede73eb71f647bb6ac1b8bfbb2c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Which install-local uninstalls are now refused.** `handleUninstall` (plugin l.3340) asks, in this order: capability admission → `manifestId` present → ledger `has` (404 otherwise) → walled-catalog refusal (403) → **new: `askUninstallGuards`** → registry `assertPackageUninstallable` (409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`) → `ledger.remove` (first write). So exactly the uninstalls a registered pre-uninstall guard refuses are newly refused, and only for a ledgered package. Today's one guard is the runtime's `runtime.package-dependent-rules` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` l.982–991): a package whose `objectExtensions` field an active validation rule of another enabled package reads → `409 PACKAGE_DISABLE_RESTRICTED_BY_VALIDATION_RULE` with `disableDependentRulesMessage(..., { operation: 'uninstall' })`. The door answers `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }` under the guard's `status`, the same body shape as its other refusals. Nothing withdrawn, nothing written: the refusal returns before `ledger.read`/`ledger.remove`, `captureUninstallDeclared`, `withdrawFromRunningKernel`, the object-copy withdrawal, the cleanups, the re-sync and the audit write. The door test pins exactly this (ledger entry kept, package registered, field served, `runUninstallCleanups` not called, no audit event).
- **One `package_uninstall` row per passing uninstall.** `recordUninstall` is called once, after the re-sync, on the one success path; every refusal above returns earlier and the one failure path (`ledger.remove` throws → 500) returns before it. The row is `{ action: 'package_uninstall', packageId, version? (read from the ledger entry before its removal), environmentId? (the protocol's), actor? (`admission.userId`), itemsRemoved: 0, itemsFailed: 0 }`. No `audit` slot → nothing written, never thrown (`writePackageUninstallEvent` returns on a missing `recordPackageLifecycleEvent`; a slot that throws is logged). CONTROL case of the door test pins exactly one event.
- **`deletePackage` is behaviourally identical after the refactor.** Read side by side at the head: (a) guard step — was `await askUninstallGuards(this.uninstallGuards, request)`, now `await runUninstallGuards.call(this, request)`, whose whole body is that same call; `askUninstallGuards`'s body is untouched (only its parameter type narrowed to a Pick of DeletePackageRequest's `packageId` and `actor`, the two keys it ever read); same position (first thing after the retired-key refusal, before the `sys_metadata` read); same throw shape (`Error` with `code`, `status`, `message`). (b) audit step — same guard condition `installed.held`, or at least one deleted or failed item, same position (after `runUninstallCleanups`), and the event `writePackageUninstallEvent` receives has the same keys in the same order with the same inclusion conditions (`version` when truthy, `environmentId` when truthy, `actor` when truthy, `keepData` only when `=== true`, both counts). The `this` handed to `recordPackageUninstall.call(this, ...)` inside the verb is the verb's host, whose `environmentId`/`getServicesRegistry` getters are the ones the old inline write read. The existing #31232 / #31186 `deletePackage` cases stay in the suite unchanged.
- **One verdict, one writer.** The door holds no copy: `askUninstallGuards` (plugin) only calls `protocol.runUninstallGuards`; `recordUninstall` only calls `protocol.recordPackageUninstall`. In the protocol the guard loop exists once (module-private `askUninstallGuards`) and the slot write once (module-private `writePackageUninstallEvent`); both public members and the verb reach those two functions. The class members' host literals use the same reader-closure pattern as `deletePackage` and `resolveFlowCanonicalizer`; `getServicesRegistry` is a stored constructor closure, so calling it on the host literal is sound.
- **Capability question.** `UninstallCleanupRunner` gains `runUninstallGuards?` / `recordPackageUninstall?` typed as indexed accesses on `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (not restated). A protocol without either member is not asked and the door behaves as before — consistent with the existing `runUninstallCleanups` probe.

### ② Semver level

- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, line-initial, identical. `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes (narrowing)` as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another", which is what the prose "both arms" states. The narrowing arm is right: `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/:manifestId` now answers 409 for an uninstall it answered 200 — a consumer-visible accept-set shrink, so BREAKING: `!` in the title, the **BREAKING** banner and the FROM/NOW/remedy paragraphs are present, and the changeset carries one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), as item 3 of AGENTS.md requires of a breaking changeset.
- **Widening arm — reachability.** `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` is exported from `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` l.3 and `exports["."]` maps to `dist/index.d.ts`, so the two new unmodified (public) methods are published accept set, not shipped bytes. `PackageUninstallRecord` is exported as a type at `index.ts` l.138 (and re-exported through `protocol.ts`), so it is reachable too. Hence `yes` is required; the claim's `no (narrowing)` would have been wrong for this diff and the dev's re-declaration is correct.
- **Level under ruling A (#25105).** `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes (no spec key, value or type; the refusal is a runtime verdict at a door). AGENTS.md item 3: "`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition." So `@objectstack/cloud-connection: patch` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` are the ruled levels; `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green on the head.
- **Prose faces agree with the code.** The changeset's Before/Now/Unchanged match ①. The handbook paragraph (step 9) states the 409 code, "naming the rule" (the sentence names it), "nothing is removed", and "the same refusal `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` answers" (`packages.ts` l.945 says so). Nit: it says a completed uninstall "is recorded in the audit log" without the changeset's qualifier "a runtime with no audit plugin writes no row".

### ③ Boundary flags

- Report 6719019099: `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no extra author note owed.
- Deviation 1 — `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx` outside the order's surface: prose face, declared on the `Skills-docs:` line, agrees with the code (② above). Accepted.
- Deviation 2 — Clause-② moved from the claim's `no (narrowing)` to `yes (narrowing)`: correct, see ②.
- Deviation 3 — one merge of `origin/main` (645c9512); main moved 11 commits after, not re-merged: verified that none of those commits touch the nine files, so the net diff against today's `main` is the PR's own. #31402 / #31398 (same file, other hunks) still open: unchanged serial note, nothing to escalate here.

The report also says the CI families were left to the seat; this is one of them.
- Route choice ("why not delegate"): verified against the verb at the head. For a package with no stored rows `deletePackage` would (step 4) hand `packageStore.delete(packageId)` an id the store never held and throw `packagePersistFailureError` on a returned/thrown refusal, answer `success: false` (`deleted.length === 0`) otherwise, drop object tables by default, and skip the door's ledger/copy/re-sync steps — so public entry points are the right route, and no `packages/spec` member is involved (both live on the class only, like `runUninstallCleanups`), so no `needs_decision` was owed.
- **Check-runs on 645c9512 at 2026-11-08T08:08Z** (read by `gh api`): 22 completed success (among them Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, both scoped lints, Test UI, Build Docs, Type Check · source gates / debt ledger), 12 skipped (opt-in/UI matrices), **2 failure: `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and its aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates`**, 12 still in progress (Build Core, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8–8/8, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace). The red is PR-introduced, not a merge-base signature: the same job is green on the merge-base 383c3530 and on the base head 18ed2db1 (job 128669971074).

### ④ Design judgment

1. **must-fix — the two new facade members hold bodies the facade gate refuses; the head is red on `check:facade-delegation-only`.** `scripts/facade-delegation-registry.json` registers `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (card #29985) as delegation-only; `judgeDelegationBody` accepts `const host = {...}; return fn.call(host, ...)` but not an object literal built inline as the `.call` argument (self-test H5). (2 statement(s))", "recordPackageUninstall ... (3 statement(s))". Fix in either accepted shape: (a) bind the host literal to a `const host` typed as the function's ThisParameterType, holding the literal, and `return runUninstallGuards.call(host, request)` exactly as `deletePackage` (l.11014) and `resolveFlowCanonicalizer` (l.941) do; or (b) move the two bodies into `ProtocolClassHeadFacet` beside `runUninstallCleanups` and `registerUninstallGuard` and delegate `return ProtocolClassHeadFacet.x(protocolHost(this), ...)`. No exceptions row is warranted (the bodies can move). Behaviour is unchanged by either; the gate, not the semantics, is what fails. Must-fix because the diff reds a repo gate that is green on its merge-base, which blocks landing (② all checks green) and breaks the #29985 facade rule the committed registry enforces.
2. **nit — refusal status window at the door.** `askUninstallGuards` answers a thrown refusal only when `code` is a string and `status` is in the 400–499 range; anything else propagates. The verb's REST door renders every throw through `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 500)`, which honours the thrown `status`. A guard refusing with a non-4xx status (the `UninstallGuardRefusal` type allows any number) would thus be answered as spelled at `DELETE /packages/:id` but surface as an unhandled throw at install-local. Not reachable today (the only guard answers 409) and the PR declares this exact behaviour, so no contract effect.
3. **nit — the door's row cannot say the uninstall was partial.** `itemsRemoved: 0, itemsFailed: 0` is always written, including when the registry withdrawal or a cleanup failed (those ride on `cleanups`). The verb's row has the same blind spot for its own withdrawal and cleanups (it counts only `sys_metadata` item failures, of which this door has none), so parity holds; accepted deviation, documented beside the call.
4. Guard runs before the door's first write — confirmed (①). After the guard resolves, the path to `ledger.remove` and `registry.uninstallPackage` is synchronous (registry predicate, `ledger.read`, `ledger.remove`, `captureUninstallDeclared`, `withdrawFromRunningKernel`), so no other request interleaves between verdict and withdrawal; tighter than the verb, which awaits a store read in between. Concurrency with the cleanups is unchanged from #21490.
5. A guard that needs the package still registered — satisfied: the runtime guard resolves `objectql.registry` at ask time and the door asks before withdrawal, under the same id (`manifestId`) that `assertPackageUninstallable` and `uninstallPackage` use. A package the kernel never registered (the `withdrawal`-outcome case) yields no dependents and passes, as it would through the verb.
6. Actor / organization — `admission.userId` (the authenticated principal) is the actor, as the pair-install undo in this file already passes to `deletePackage`; the verb's door passes `resolvePackageWriteActor`. The row carries the protocol's `environmentId` and no organization on both doors (ADR-0131: an uninstall is environment-wide), so parity holds.
7. Uninstall that fails after guards pass — `ledger.remove` throws → 500, nothing moved, no row (the package stays installed; correct). Past that point the uninstall is durable; failures are outcomes on `cleanups` and one row is still written, as the verb writes after its `sys_packages` delete regardless of per-item failures. The writer never throws for slot faults.
8. Cloud vs inline branch — the split is on install (cloud-fetched vs inline manifest); both write a ledger entry and the one uninstall door is keyed on the ledger, so guards and row cover both. The pair-install undo reaches the guards through `deletePackage` itself.
9. Guard throws vs refuses — a guard's own throw (no `code`/`status`) propagates out of the door exactly as out of the verb; an uninstall a guard could not judge does not proceed and nothing has moved.
10. Tests — door test is a real `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` + `AppPlugin` (the real guard registration) with a recorder `audit` slot; the four protocol cases pin the runner's throw/pass-through and the writer's event/no-slot paths. Dev-reported red-on-main and two ablations are consistent with the hunks but were not re-run here (read-only).
